name: Nine Card Brag
description: Nine Card Brag (often called 'Crash') is the final evolution of the multi-card Brag family. Players are dealt nine cards and must divide them into three independent three-card hands. These hands are compared against opponents' corresponding hands in three separate 'showdowns' (front, middle, and back). It combines the traditional British Brag hand rankings with the partition complexity of Chinese Poker, creating a high-stakes duel of distribution and nerve.

overview.description: Nine Card Brag (often called 'Crash') is the final evolution of the multi-card Brag family. Players are dealt nine cards and must divide them into three independent three-card hands. These hands are compared against opponents' corresponding hands in three separate 'showdowns' (front, middle, and back). It combines the traditional British Brag hand rankings with the partition complexity of Chinese Poker, creating a high-stakes duel of distribution and nerve.

history.origins: Originating in the card rooms of Northern England and Scotland, 9-Card Brag emerged as a more complex alternative to the simpler vying variants. It likely took inspiration from the global 'partition' genre while strictly adhering to the centuries-old Brag combination hierarchy.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-hand Brag variants evolve in British social clubs.
1970s: The name 'Crash' becomes synonymous with the 13-card and 9-card partition versions.
Present: A competitive staple in the UK Brag community, often played for high stakes.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Professional' version of Brag, where the luck of the draw is minimized by the skill of the partition.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a vying focus (betting) toward a scoring focus (winning individual hand comparisons), although many gambling variants still include an initial betting round.

setup.dealing: Deal nine cards face-down to each player. Players then divide their hand into three separate 3-card Brag combinations.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, score pad or chips.

rules.objective: Win the majority of the three hand comparisons against your opponents.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partition**: Players divide 9 cards into Hand 1, Hand 2, and Hand 3. 2. **Ordering**: Some variants require hands to be ordered from strongest to weakest. 3. **Comparison**: Hands are revealed one at a time. The winner of each comparison (e.g., Hand 1 vs. Hand 1) scores a point. 4. **Ranks**: Prial (3-3-3 is highest) > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: All three hands must be valid Brag combinations.
A player who wins all three comparisons is said to have 'Crashed' or 'Swept', often winning a bonus.
Tied comparisons usually result in the point being carried over or shared.

strategy.basic: Don't put all your best cards in one hand. Winning one comparison and losing two will lose you the round. Aim for three balanced 'Pairs' rather than one 'Prial' and two junk hands.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Middle' Trap: Many players put their second-best cards in the middle hand. If you put your best cards in the middle, you can often steal a point from someone who played traditionally.
strategy.advanced: Range Splitting: Evaluate the deck's remaining strength. If you hold many Spades, expect opponents to be weak in sequences and strong in pairs. Adjust your partition to beat pairs with low sequences (Runs).
tips: In 9-Card Brag, a Flush is a 'medium' hand; don't rely on it to win the front hand.
Count the Aces—there are only four. If you have two, the odds of an opponent holding a Prial of Aces is near zero.

variations.name: Crash (13-Card)
variations.description: Players receive 13 cards and form four Brag hands, leaving one card as a muck.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation links the related 13-card Crash game; engine overrides for that larger partition are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Points are awarded for each winning hand comparison. Bonus points for winning all three (the Crash).
scoring.winCondition: Win the majority of hand comparisons in the round.

synthesis.shortDescription: The strategic peak of the Brag family. Partition nine cards into three independent units and face your opponent across three simultaneous showdowns. Master the math of the split and the bluff of the front hand to become the ultimate Nine Card champion.
